newsitem.title: USA: U.S. corporate bonds inactive, seen cautiously bid.
newsitem.headline: U.S. corporate bonds inactive, seen cautiously bid.

text.p: U.S. investment grade corporate bond investors made few active markets on Friday as a double-dose of strong economic data sent prices lower, dealers said.

Markets for some of the more than $3.0 billion in fresh supply either held in or widened marginally, reflecting a cautiously firm bid amid the rising rates. J.C. Penney's five-year tranche widened one basis point from Thursday at 47 bid, but remained well inside its issued level of 50 basis points over the Treasury curve.

But overall activity remained quiet after a strong revision to February retail sales data and surprising jump in March core wholesale prices conspired to bolster speculation the Federal Reserve will raise short-term interest rates at its May open market committee meeting.

Treasury and equity markets broke sharply lower following the data, with stocks falling precipitously near their closes. The 30-year bond was quoted down 21/32 to yield 7.17 percent in late trade. The Dow closed down 148 points at 6391 and the Nasdaq was off 29 to 1207.

Stock selling fostered a heavier tone in high-yield bonds but trading there was light and levels were hard to guage on a broad basis. But some players were encouraged by a slowdown in redemptions seen in junk bond funds seen over the past month.

Net cash outflows from high-yield funds were $172.6 million in the week ended April 9 compared with outflows of $663.2 million one week prior, according to AMG Data Services. Total redemptions from high-yield funds total more than $1.57 billion since the trend turned negative in mid-March.
High-yield issuance on Friday was led by $150 million 11-1/2 percent 10-year B3/B-minus senior notes from Greyhound Lines Inc, priced at par via lead manager Bear Stearns & Co.
The notes were seen trading on both sides of par late in the session, one trader said.
Other junk bond issues included:
--$120 million 10-year 11-1/4 percent B2/B-minus senior
subordinated notes at par from MMI Products Inc via Bear
Stearns;
--$115 million seven-year 11-1/4 percent B2/single-B first
mortgage notes at par from Sun World International Inc
via Salomon Brothers;
--and $155 million seven-year 12-1/2 percent B2/B-minus
senior secured notes from Panda Global Holdings Inc,
priced to yield 14 percent via Donaldson, Lufkin &
Jenrette.
Looking ahead, players said high-yield conferences held by Donaldson, Lufkin & Jenrette and Bear, Stearns next week would be certain to cap new issue and secondary activity.
